slides.heading: One giant prompt will fail your workflow
slides.body: We tried using a single prompt to research, draft, edit, and design content. It failed consistently. Here is what we learned from rebuilding it.

slides.heading: Split the work into specialized agents
slides.body: We replaced our single prompt with seven task-specific agents. One drafts, one checks citations, one guards tone, and one formats text. Accuracy improved the moment each agent received one job.

slides.heading: Match models to operational needs
slides.body: Heavy reasoning tasks run on Gemini 3.1 Pro. Fast, repetitive tasks run on Gemini 3.8 Flash. Assigning models based on role keeps costs down without dropping quality.

slides.heading: Build automatic retries and failovers
slides.body: Endpoints flake during long generations. If our social copy agent fails, it retries twice before failing over to a larger model. The screen never displays half-written data.

slides.heading: Let code handle the visual design
slides.body: Brand consistency drifts when models manage layout. Our agents return raw text in structured JSON. A deterministic code renderer maps that text directly into fixed brand templates.

slides.heading: Shift the operator to reviewer
slides.body: Automation handles drafting and layout. Every final asset drops into an approval queue. The human operator never writes from scratch, but always gives the final sign-off.

slides.heading: Keep your system modular
slides.body: Save this post for the next time you design an automated content pipeline.
